title.value: Predicting the probability distribution of bus travel time to measure the reliability of public transport services
title.justification: The title explicitly states the focus of the paper is on predicting the probability distribution of bus travel time to assess public transport reliability.
title.quote: Predicting the probability distribution of bus travel time to measure the reliability of public transport services

extractions.description: The paper empirically compares probabilistic models for predicting the conditional probability density function (PDF) of bus travel time to evaluate public transport reliability. It tests similarity-based density estimation and a smoothed logistic regression model on a dataset from 50 bus routes in Montréal.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving public transport reliability through probabilistic travel time predictions, rather than addressing climate change directly.
climate_change_is_central.quote: An important aspect of the quality of a public transport service is its reliability, which is defined as the invariability of the service attributes. In order to measure reliability during the service planning phase, a key piece of information is the long-term prediction of the density of the travel time, which conveys the uncertainty of travel times.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus on transport reliability and predictive modeling doesn't directly align with climate change mitigation, adaptation, or other sustainability categories.
primary_category.quote: This work empirically compares probabilistic models for the prediction of the conditional probability density function (PDF) of the travel time and proposes a simulation framework taking as input the latter distributions to approximate the expected secondary delays, a measure of the reliability of public transport services.

secondary_categories.justification: Though not central, improving public transport reliability can indirectly reduce emissions by encouraging public transport use over personal vehicles.
secondary_categories.quote: In order to increase ridership and attract new users, public transport agencies put increasing emphasis on improving the quality of the service they provide and particularly its regularity, also referred to as reliability.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not focus on a specific climate change sub-category as its primary theme is transport reliability, not explicitly linked to any listed sub-categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: This model reduced the mean squared error of the expected secondary delay by approximately 9% compared to the benchmark model, namely a random forest.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper involves public transportation, which can be linked to climate change efforts to reduce emissions by promoting efficient public transit.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This work aims at providing tools to measure, and eventually improve, the reliability of one of the outputs of the service planning phase, namely vehicle schedules.

applications.value: Improving public transport service reliability to increase ridership, which might encourage a modal shift from private vehicles to public transport, indirectly supporting emission reductions.
applications.justification: Enhanced reliability of public transport could shift more people from using personal vehicles to opting for buses, reducing carbon emissions.
applications.quote: In order to increase ridership and attract new users, public transport agencies put increasing emphasis on improving the quality of the service they provide and particularly its regularity, also referred to as reliability.

new_primary_category.justification: Existing categories did not fit as the primary focus is on public transport reliability, not climate change.
new_primary_category.quote: This work empirically compares probabilistic models for the prediction of the conditional probability density function (PDF) of the travel time and proposes a simulation framework taking as input the latter distributions to approximate the expected secondary delays.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is needed as the focus on public transport reliability falls outside the specific climate change categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This model reduced the mean squared error of the expected secondary delay by approximately 9% compared to the benchmark model, namely a random forest.
